skill.name: slideshow
skill.description: Create HyperFrames slideshow decks with discrete slides, fragments, branching hotspots, presenter mode, speaker notes, and validation guidance.
skill.summary: Create interactive HyperFrames slideshow decks with navigation, branching, fragments, and presenter mode.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code formatting, local relative paths, media object keys, and presentation guidance. One low-severity issue remains: the standalone Three.js example imports a public CDN module, which can introduce a runtime network and supply-chain dependency if copied.

remediation.issue: Optional standalone Three.js example uses a public CDN import.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer vendoring Three.js or documenting a local asset path so generated decks do not depend on runtime external network access.

content.value_statement: Building a HyperFrames deck requires careful scene timing, navigation structure, and presenter handoff. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to author runnable slideshow decks with validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Defines the HyperFrames slideshow JSON island for slide order, notes, fragments, hotspots, and branch sequences.
Explains how to structure scenes with matching data-composition-id values and timing attributes.
Guides conversion of existing pages into slide-based decks while preserving visual behavior and media behavior.
Documents presenter mode, audience tab sharing, editable notes, media cleanup, and global mute behavior.
Provides validation steps for linting slide references, hotspot targets, fragment timing, and runtime behavior.
limitations: It produces a runnable deck, not a single rendered MP4 export.
Engine-hosted slideshow preview is described as future work, so standalone demos need interim wrapper patterns.
Text-to-speech manifest fields are reserved and not wired for playback.
It assumes the user is working inside the HyperFrames composition model.

best_practices: Confirm the user wants a HyperFrames slideshow before authoring a deck from an adjacent presentation request.
Keep each slide focused on one complete-sentence claim and one visual idea.
Run HyperFrames lint and validation before handoff, then provide presenter-mode instructions.
anti_patterns: Do not render the deck as a single MP4 because branch slides and timing can be lost.
Do not hide the slideshow manifest behind runtime-generated JSON.
Do not add one-off media cleanup, mute, or note-editing scripts when the shared slideshow player owns those behaviors.

faq.question: Does this skill create video exports?
faq.answer: No. It creates runnable HyperFrames slideshow decks. The skill warns that rendering to one MP4 can truncate the deck.

faq.question: Can it create branching presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents hotspot targets and slide sequences for optional branch paths.

faq.question: Does it support presenter notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the shared presenter view with editable notes stored locally per deck and slide.

faq.question: Can it convert an existing page?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes rules for preserving source design, motion, media behavior, and camera transitions.

faq.question: What should users validate before handoff?
faq.answer: Users should run lint and runtime validation, then confirm navigation, fragments, hotspots, presenter mode, and media behavior.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
